questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between phosphorus mineralisation and immobilisation. [K] / [CO2]

  • inorganic phosphate. In contrast, phosphorus immobilisation is the reverse process, in which soil
  • microbes absorb inorganic phosphate and convert it into organic forms.

questions.question: What are epiphytic and endophytic microorganisms? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What are epiphytic and endophytic microorganisms? [K] / [CO2]
  • Plant-associated microbes that differ primarily by where they live relative to the host plant.
  • Epiphytic Microorganisms (Epiphytes)
  • They live on the external surface of plants (such as leaves, stems, flowers, and fruits)
  • Endophytic Microorganisms (Endophytes)
  • They live inside the internal tissues of plants (such as within cells, intercellular spaces, or the
  • vascular system) without causing visible disease.

  • woody stem.

  • enzymes. Direct chemical breakdown using agents like sodium hydroxide.

questions.question: Distinguish between ectomycorrhiza and endomycorrhiza. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Distinguish between ectomycorrhiza and endomycorrhiza. [U] / [CO1] Key Differences Feature Ectomycorrhiza Endomycorrhiza (Arbuscular) Colonization Extracellular: Fungi stay outside the root cells. Intracellular: Fungi penetrate inside the root cortical cells. Outer Sheath Forms a dense outer fungal covering called a mantle. Does not form a mantle. Internal Network Forms an intercellular network between cells called the Hartig net. Forms tree-like arbuscules and storage vesicles inside the cells. Fungal Partners Mostly Basidiomycota and Ascomycota. Mostly Glomeromycota. Plant Hosts Found in about 3%–10% of plants, mainly woody trees like pines, oaks, and spruces (conifers and hardwoods). Found in about 80%–85% of plants, including most crops, grasses, vegetables, and flowers. Root Alteration Often makes the roots look swollen, stunted, or coral-like. Does not change the outer shape of the roots. Lab Culture Can generally be grown (cultured) in a lab. Cannot be cultured independently without a living host plant (obligate symbionts). Any three points.
